sections.html:
Magna is a city in Salt Lake County on the west side of the valley, just northeast of the Oquirrh Mountains and directly south of the Great Salt Lake. Its elevation is about 4,265 feet.

On the valley grid it sits between roughly 7200 and 9200 West and 2100 and 4100 South. Coon Creek drains from Coon Canyon and flows northwest through town toward the lake. SR-201 forms the northern edge as an expressway and meets I-80 to the west.

The lake and the mountains give Magna a different feel from the east side of the valley. Wind, dust and salt air are part of the setting, and a house near the northern boundary is closer to the lake than one in the southern subdivisions.

sections.h2: How did a copper mill town become a city?
sections.html:
Magna began as a farming and ranching settlement and grew into a company town for copper processing. Pioneers started arriving in 1851, Abraham Coon ran a livestock ranch at the mouth of what is now Coon Canyon, and the community was first called Pleasant Green in 1868.

The turning point came in 1906, when D.C. Jackling's Utah Copper Company began construction of the Magna Mill. Jackling chose the name from the Latin word for great. The post office was renamed Magna in 1914, and the name was officially adopted on October 19, 1915.

  • 1903: Greek immigration began.
  • 1909: Boston Consolidated built a second mill, and the two companies merged in 1911.
  • 1924: the first building of Cyprus High School was completed.
  • 2001: Magna gained township status.
  • 2017: it became a metro township.
  • May 1, 2024: it became a city under Utah House Bill 35.

Older neighborhoods around Main Street carried names such as Greektown, Japantown, Snaketown and Little Italy. Newer single-family subdivisions went up south and east of the historic center during the 1970s.

sections.h2: How big is Magna, and how fast is it growing?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 29,251 people in Magna, up 10.4 percent from 26,505 in 2010. The Census Bureau's estimate for July 1, 2025 is 35,401.

Earlier census counts show how the town developed: 3,502 in 1950, 13,138 in 1980, 17,629 in 1990 and 22,770 in 2000. In 2020, about 56.2 percent of residents were non-Hispanic white and 34.4 percent were Hispanic or Latino of any race.

Housing built in the 1970s is now fifty years old, and sellers of those homes often face the same list of age-related repairs, such as roofs, furnaces, windows and aging plumbing.

sections.h2: What was the March 2020 earthquake, and why does it matter to a Magna seller?
sections.html:
A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck at 7:09 a.m. on March 18, 2020, with its epicenter about 6 kilometers north-northeast of Magna. It was the strongest earthquake in Utah since the 1992 St. George earthquake, and it was the first major earthquake in the Salt Lake Valley since the city was founded.

No deaths were reported and injuries were minor. Bricks fell from some buildings, about 145 historic structures were damaged, and Cyprus High School suffered some of the most significant damage. The Magna town page counts more than 850 aftershocks, while the earthquake article notes 591 located by March 26. Building-related damage was put at about $62 million out of $629 million in total economic losses.

The quake was consistent with movement on the Wasatch Fault system at depth. Buyers and inspectors in Magna often look at chimneys, foundations and masonry for cracks, and a seller who has had repairs done should keep the paperwork. A house with leftover damage is one reason owners consider selling as-is.

sections.h2: What are the main employers and development plans in Magna?
sections.html:
Copper mining drove Magna's economy for most of a century. The mills shut during the Great Depression and revived around 1940 with wartime demand, and Hercules Powder began producing rocket motors at its Bacchus Works plant south of town. Northrop Grumman now operates a solid rocket motor manufacturing plant in Magna.

Kennecott Land's West Bench plan calls for major development, including an urban center along I-80. Main Street has seen commercial decline and some vacant storefronts, though it was remodeled in 2006 and is a popular filming location.

Plans for a large new development nearby can change what buyers expect in the area, though nothing in the sources gives a date or price effect. Sellers who are unsure should compare a recent nearby sale rather than guess.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools serve Magna?
sections.html:
The main east and west road is West 3500 South (SR-171), and the main north and south road is South 8400 West (SR-111). UTA route 35 runs along 3500 South every 15 minutes on weekdays and loops through Main Street, and the TRAX Green Line is nearby.

Magna is in the Granite School District. Elementary schools are Copper Hills, Elk Run, Lake Ridge, Magna and Pleasant Green. Matheson Junior High is the middle school, and Cyprus High School competes at the 5A level. Brockbank Junior High closed in 2016 and merged into the Cyprus High campus.

sections.h2: Who handles code enforcement and building permits in Magna?
sections.html:
The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District, known as the MSD, serves Magna City along with Kearns, Copperton, White City, Emigration Canyon, Brighton and unincorporated Salt Lake County. It provides planning and zoning, building permits and inspections, code enforcement and business licensing. It does not provide police, fire or sanitation.

The MSD code enforcement page lists the types of violations it handles:

  • Weeds taller than six inches
  • Outdoor storage of junk
  • Parking on dirt or grass
  • More than two unregistered or inoperable vehicles on a property
  • Unpermitted signs, home businesses or short-term rentals
  • Exceeding the number of unrelated occupants
  • Setback violations, such as carports too close to a property line

Construction without a permit goes to the MSD Building Department at (385) 468-6688. Code enforcement is at 860 W Levoy Drive, Suite 300, Taylorsville, and the phone is (385) 910-5780. The page does not say when each rule was last changed, so owners should call to confirm.

sections.h2: How do Salt Lake County tax dates and recording work for a Magna sale?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County tax notices are mailed by November 1, taxes are due November 30, unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty rises after January 31. The Auditor sends the tax sale listing on March 15, and the final tax sale takes place on the fourth Thursday of May.

The Salt Lake County Recorder is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, Salt Lake City, and can be reached at 385-468-8145, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The county's Property Watch service sends alerts to help protect a property. A guide for handling property after an owner's death is also posted for residents.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Magna house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Magna ends with the same title company closing and recorded deed as any other sale, without a lender's appraisal and underwriting. The seller shares the address and condition, reviews the buyer's offer and signs a purchase contract.

  • Gather the deed or trust papers, and any code notices.
  • Ask the title company to confirm liens and taxes.
  • Pick a closing date that works around any repairs or move-out plans.

Owners with earthquake-related repairs left undone, inherited houses or code notices from the MSD are among those who consider this path.

faqs.a: Yes. Magna became a city on May 1, 2024, under Utah House Bill 35. It had been a township from 2001 and a metro township from 2017.

faqs.q: How many people live in Magna?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 35,401 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 29,251.

faqs.q: Who handles code enforcement for a Magna house?
faqs.a: The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District. Call (385) 910-5780 for code enforcement or (385) 468-6688 for building and construction without a permit.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due November 30. Unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty increases after January 31.

faqs.q: Did the 2020 earthquake damage homes in Magna?
faqs.a: Some buildings were damaged. The magnitude 5.7 quake on March 18, 2020 had its epicenter about 6 kilometers north-northeast of Magna, and building-related damage was estimated at about $62 million.
